card.name: Pronoun starting a reported clause
card.fires_on: A pronoun such as her, I, she, him, you or my that begins the subject of a clause after a speech or thought verb plus "that" (told, announces, described). It also fires on a pronoun after a linking phrase like "must" or "like Henry Louis Gates,".

modes.label: After told/announces that
modes.description: A subject pronoun or possessive opens a clause reporting what someone said or learned.
modes.example: I’m not diabetic, but my doctor told me that<< I>> have gestational diabetes.

modes.label: Pronoun after other linkers
modes.description: A pronoun follows a preposition, modal or comparison phrase and refers back to a person.
modes.example: In "Faces of America," Elizabeth Alexander, poet and Yale professor of African American and gender studies, learned that, like Henry Louis Gates,<< she>> is genetically more European
